links.outcome: AUC of ML model versus ophthalmologists and Ocular Trauma Score on same cases
links.effect: VisionGo AUC 0.75 and 0.90 vs OTS 0.49; vs ophthalmologists 0.73 vs 0.57 (previtrectomy) and 0.87 vs 0.64 (intravitrectomy)
links.quote: VisionGo showed better performance than ophthalmologists in both previtrectomy and intravitrectomy application scenarios (AUC=0.73 vs 0.57 and 0.87 vs 0.64).

links.outcome: Performance in small prospective real-world validation versus retrospective testing
links.effect: Previtrectomy AUC fell from 0.75 to 0.60 in prospective validation (27 cases); intravitrectomy AUC stayed similar (0.90 vs 0.91).
links.quote: In real-world validation, VisionGo achieved an AUC of 0.60 and 0.91 in previtrectomy and intravitrectomy application scenarios.

unlisted_practices: SHAP feature-contribution analysis for model interpretability

screen.reason: The study develops and tests a predictive risk model (VisionGo) compared to ophthalmologists and standard scores on retrospective data and a small prospective cohort, but it evaluates model performance rather than testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
